stage: module asset closure, derived the way the compiler derives it
why: a module manifest declares its asset ids and its sourceFiles; if a declared asset had no definition, or a definition pointed at a binary that is not on disk, the compiler would fail the pack (or the game would show a missing image) - so the closure was checked
the_false_positive_I_avoided: my first scan collected records by a kind field equal to 'asset' and reported EIGHT declared assets as UNDEFINED. That was MY bug: the compiler takes the kind from the ID (KindFromId) rather than from a kind field, so records shaped with kind 'image' but an id containing :asset/ were skipped by my filter. Collected by ID instead, all thirty-three are defined
measured: thirty-three asset ids declared across the module manifests, THIRTY-THREE defined in their own sourceFiles, FIVE of them pointing at real binaries that all exist, and ZERO problems
why_not_vacuous: the check also asserts that at least one asset points at a real binary, so it cannot pass on an empty set, and that the declared count is still thirty-three
boundary: this covers assets under the module folders; the campaign-level photoBook facts and photos are checked by the book projection instead

verified.not_run: no game launch: seeing an image render is visual acceptance
